extracted.intended_audience: teachers, teacher-educators, and students of pedagogy
extracted.subtask_description: Principles and criteria for pedagogical method: how subject-matter and method should be integrated, what constitutes an effective educative situation, and the personal intellectual traits teachers should cultivate and promote in pupils.

rubrics_metrics.name: Essentials of method (reflective situation)
rubrics_metrics.description: First, that the pupil have a genuine situation of experience—that there be a continuous activity in which he is interested for its own sake; secondly, that a genuine problem develop within this situation as a stimulus to thought; third, that he possess the information and make the observations needed to deal with it; fourth, that suggested solutions occur to him which he shall be responsible for developing in an orderly way; fifth, that he have opportunity and occasion to test his ideas by application, to make their meaning clear and to discover for himself their validity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These five steps are presented as the essentials of method and of reflection: set up an authentic experience, let a problem arise, ensure relevant information/observation, foster student-generated solutions that the pupil must develop, and provide occasions to test and apply ideas. This sequence is the model of educative thinking and should be embodied in instructional practice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unity of subject matter and method
rubrics_metrics.description: Method means that arrangement of subject matter which makes it most effective in use. Method is not something external to the material; it is the effective direction of subject matter to desired results.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reject the dualistic view that subject matter is a ready-made body and method is merely a set of external techniques. Method should be conceived as the shaping and ordering of material toward ends; teaching must integrate content and method rather than treat them as separable domains.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use lessons to establish cross-connections (avoid isolated lessons)
rubrics_metrics.description: The least desirable treats each lesson as an independent whole. Wiser teachers see to it that the student is systematically led to utilize his earlier lessons to help understand the present one, and also to use the present to throw additional light upon what has already been acquired.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Every recitation offers opportunity to connect subject matter to wider experiences and to prior learning; failure to do so leaves out-of-school experience crude and unrefined. Teachers should habitually prompt students to find points of contact and mutual bearings between lessons and real-life situations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Derive methods from concrete situations and empirical study of cases
rubrics_metrics.description: There can be no discovery of a method without cases to be studied. The method is derived from observation of what actually happens, with a view to seeing that it happen better next time.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Methods should emerge from study of successes and failures in real situations rather than be handed down as rote prescriptions. Overreliance on authoritative recipes produces mechanical uniformity and ignores individual variation; teachers should observe, compare cases, and formulate method from that empirical base.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid reducing method to cut-and-dried routine
rubrics_metrics.description: Method tends to be reduced to a cut and dried routine, to following mechanically prescribed steps... Instead of being encouraged to attack their topics directly, experimenting with methods that seem promising and learning to discriminate by the consequences that accrue, it is assumed that there is one fixed method to be followed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Steer clear of imposing preordained verbal formulae or rigid sequences of steps. Encourage experimentation, judgment, and flexible adjustment of procedures to fit the unique demands of each situation; recognize that mechanized methods stifle initiative and adaptability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Know and use general (established) methods while adapting them to the individual case
rubrics_metrics.description: There exists a cumulative body of fairly stable methods for reaching results, a body authorized by past experience and by intellectual analysis... To be used intelligently, existing practices, however authorized they may be, have to be adapted to the exigencies of particular cases.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Teach and learn established techniques as intellectual aids—standpoints for inquiry—not as rigid models. Use knowledge of past practices to suggest what to look into and which measures to try, but adapt them to the particulars of the learner and situation (illustrated by the physician example).

rubrics_metrics.name: Directness (trait of individual method)
rubrics_metrics.description: Directness denotes the straightforwardness with which one goes at what he has to do; it is easier to indicate through negatives—self-consciousness, embarrassment, and constraint are its menacing foes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Foster confidence (not reflexive self-consciousness) and whole-hearted engagement. Avoid instructional practices that draw pupils' attention away from the matter at hand or induce self-conscious performance; such practices impair directness and produce divided, inefficient attention.

rubrics_metrics.name: Open-mindedness (trait of individual method)
rubrics_metrics.description: Openness of mind means accessibility of mind to any and every consideration that will throw light upon the situation that needs to be cleared up, and that will help determine the consequences of acting this way or that.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Encourage intellectual hospitality—welcome alien points of view and information that may modify purposes. Resist pressures for uniformity, quick external results, and a zeal for immediate answers which foster rigid methods and stunt intellectual growth. Open-mindedness is not passivity; it is a receptive, critical attitude.

rubrics_metrics.name: Single-mindedness / whole-heartedness (trait of individual method)
rubrics_metrics.description: Single-mindedness is completeness of interest, unity of purpose; absorption, engrossment, full concern with subject matter for its own sake—absence of suppressed but effectual ulterior aims.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Promote intellectual integrity and sincerity; beware of conditions (stern discipline, extrinsic rewards, drill) that produce divided attention or double-mindedness. True single-mindedness involves genuine engagement with subject matter rather than merely outward compliance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Responsibility / intellectual thoroughness
rubrics_metrics.description: Responsibility as an element in intellectual attitude is the disposition to consider in advance the probable consequences of any projected step and deliberately to accept them... Intellectual thoroughness is seeing a thing through.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cultivate standards that require students to follow up and act upon the meaning of what is acquired; prioritize deep understanding and conviction over superficial acquisition of many disconnected facts. Fewer well-worked-out situations are preferable to a multitude of superficially accepted truths.

rubrics_metrics.name: Motivate learning through meaningful occupations, not extrinsic rewards or coercion
rubrics_metrics.description: When the subject matter is not used in carrying forward impulses and habits to significant results, it is just something to be learned... One may utilize excitement, menace of harm, or a direct appeal to will—but these are inferior substitutes for genuine engagement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design activities where pupils are engaged for real reasons (occupation with purpose) so that learning is a by-product of meaningful activity. Avoid reliance on fear, external rewards, or drill whose sole aim is producing automatic skill—such practices foster divided interests and superficial learning.
